headlines.title: DexCom Sees Record New Patients in 2026 as Medicare Coverage Decision Looms
headlines.summary: DexCom (NASDAQ:DXCM) expects a record number of new patients in 2026 and is preparing for a potential expansion of Medicare coverage for continuous glucose monitoring, executives said during a discussion hosted by Jefferies.

headlines.title: Are Wall Street Analysts Predicting DexCom’s Stock Will Climb or Sink?
headlines.summary: Are analysts predicting CGM-maker DexCom to rise or fall?

headlines.title: Is A Medicare Delay The Biggest Risk For DexCom Stock?
headlines.summary: DexCom (DXCM) owners have one dated question left for 2026: will Medicare agree to pay for glucose monitors for people with type 2 diabetes who are not on insulin? DexCom said on its call after Q3 results that it expects CMS to announce that coverage decision this year, with DexCom's current plan assuming coverage takes effect in the middle of 2027.

headlines.title: Here's Why You Should Retain DexCom Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
headlines.summary: DexCom's G7 15 Day adoption, international expansion and margin gains support its growth prospects, though competition and rising investments pose challenges.

headlines.title: DexCom (DXCM) Could Be 32% Undervalued Following Health Canada G7 Pregnancy Clearance
headlines.summary: DexCom (DXCM) is back in focus after Health Canada cleared its G7 sensor for use with the myLoop system powered by CamAPS FX during pregnancy, creating a tightly defined new clinical use case. Recent trading tells a mixed story. The share price is up 20.75% year to date, yet the 90-day share price return is down 10.48% and the 30-day move is down 5.54%. This points to cooling momentum despite a 34.

description: DexCom, Inc., a medical device company, focuses on the design, development, and commercialization of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems for the management of diabetes and metabolic health in the United States and internationally. The company offers Dexcom G7 and G7 15 Day, an integrated continuous glucose monitoring system; Dexcom G6, a CGM system; Dexcom ONE+ to replace fingerstick blood glucose testing for diabetes treatment decisions; Stelo, a biosensor designed for adults with prediabetes and Type 2 diabetes who do not use insulin; Dexcom Share, a remote monitoring system; and Dexcom Follow application. It markets its products directly to endocrinologists, physicians, and diabetes educators. The company was incorporated in 1999 and is headquartered in San Diego, California.
